question: The pictures are already in S3, bucket permissions and CORS are set, and I trace both regular Python functions and an agent's tools. What setup remains, and what should each path record to display those pictures in Weave?
answer:
The main step left is to **register the bucket as a reference bucket for your team** in Weave. After that, each path only needs to record the picture's `s3://` URI as a plain string. Weave doesn't upload the image. When you open a trace, it creates a short-lived signed download link and shows the picture from your bucket [S1, S7].

**Remaining setup**
- Make sure you have organization admin permission. Adding a reference bucket needs the same permission as creating a team. The feature works in Multi-tenant Cloud. It's in preview for Dedicated Cloud and for Self-Managed v0.84.0+ [S6].
- Go to `https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/settings`, open **Reference buckets**, then select **Add bucket**. Choose **AWS** and enter just the bucket name, without `s3://` [S3].
- Enter the key of one object that's already in the bucket, such as `photos/cat.png`. W&B reads that object to confirm it can read the bucket and that CORS is set up correctly. You can select **Test connection** to check without saving. Then select **Add bucket** [S3].
- Until the bucket is registered, the URIs won't render as pictures. Weave only resolves URIs in buckets registered for your team [S3, S7].

**What each path should record**
- **Regular Python functions (`@weave.op`):** Put the URI string, such as `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/photos/cat.png`, in any input or output field. The field name doesn't matter, and you don't need to mark the field as media [S4, S7]. You'll see the pictures in Weave Traces.
- **Agent tools:** Inside `weave.start_conversation` → `weave.start_turn` → `weave.start_tool`, set `tool.result` to the URI string. The picture appears in the **Agents** view, on the tool call that returned it [S5, S8].

The file extension decides how the URI displays. Common image types such as `.png`, `.jpg` and `.gif` show inline. Formats Weave doesn't display inline appear as a download link [S7]. If Weave can't resolve a URI, for example because the object is missing or the bucket isn't registered, the agent view shows the plain URI text instead [S8].

# Reference media in your own bucket (BYOB) using Weave Op

> Render images and video that live in your own cloud bucket in Weave traces by logging their URIs, without importing the bytes into Weave.

Use this technique when the media you want to see in Weave already lives in your own bucket:

* Frames from a video pipeline.
* Screenshots from a browser agent.
* Images a model wrote to S3.

Instead of re-uploading those bytes into Weave, you log the object's URI as a string and Weave renders the image or video inline from your bucket. Only the URI is sent to Weave; the bytes stay in your bucket. Logging a 2 GB video costs the same as logging its path.

This is different from logging media with the [Content API](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/core-types/media.md#contents-api), which reads the bytes and stores them in Weave.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This is a Weave feature and is separate from [platform BYOB (secure storage connector)](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/secure-storage-connector.md), which backs W\&B artifact and run storage. Reference media buckets are configured per team and only need read access.

sources.heading: How it works
sources.text:
## How it works

Reference media rendering works in three steps:

1. You store a media object in your bucket, for example `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/frames/000123.png`.
2. You log that URI as a string value anywhere in a trace: an Op input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name does not matter.
3. When you open the trace, Weave resolves the URI to a short-lived [presigned URL](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/presigned-urls.md) and renders it inline. The file extension decides how it renders. Common image formats (such as `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) and video formats (such as `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.webm`) render inline. Other formats render as a download link.

Weave only resolves URIs that point at a bucket registered for your team. Supported schemes are `s3://` and `gs://`.

sources.text:
## Register the reference bucket

Register the bucket in your team settings so Weave can presign and display referenced URIs.

1. Go to your team settings page (`https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/settings`).
2. In the **Reference buckets** section, select **Add bucket**.
3. Select your cloud provider (**AWS** or **Google Cloud**).
4. For the bucket name, enter `[YOUR-BUCKET]` only — without the `s3://` or `gs://` prefix.
5. For the object key, enter the key of an existing object in the bucket, for example `photos/cat.png` (the object key only, not a full URL). W\&B reads this one object to confirm it has read access and that CORS is configured correctly. This checks access only; once verified, presigning works for any object in the bucket.
6. Optionally, select **Test connection** to validate the configuration without saving.
7. Select **Add bucket** to save.

![The Add reference bucket dialog in team settings, with fields for the cloud provider, the bucket name, and an existing object key, plus Test connection and Add bucket buttons.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/add-ref-bucket.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=7ab906b46a48b51e085530aaaf1e47a4)

>

all_read_evidence.heading: How it works
all_read_evidence.text:
## How it works

Reference media rendering works in three steps:

1. You store a media object in your bucket, for example `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/frames/000123.png`.
2. You log that URI as a string value anywhere in a trace: an Op input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name does not matter.
3. When you open the trace, Weave resolves the URI to a short-lived [presigned URL](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/presigned-urls.md) and renders it inline. The file extension decides how it renders. Common image formats (such as `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) and video formats (such as `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.webm`) render inline. Other formats render as a download link.

Weave only resolves URIs that point at a bucket registered for your team. Supported schemes are `s3://` and `gs://`.

The main step left is to **register the bucket as a reference bucket for your team** in Weave. After that, each path only needs to record the picture's `s3://` URI as a plain string. Weave doesn't upload the image. When you open a trace, it creates a short-lived signed download link and shows the picture from your bucket [S1, S7].

**Remaining setup**
- Make sure you have organization admin permission. Adding a reference bucket needs the same permission as creating a team. The feature works in Multi-tenant Cloud. It's in preview for Dedicated Cloud and for Self-Managed v0.84.0+ [S6].
- Go to `https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/settings`, open **Reference buckets**, then select **Add bucket**. Choose **AWS** and enter just the bucket name, without `s3://` [S3].
- Enter the key of one object that's already in the bucket, such as `photos/cat.png`. W&B reads that object to confirm it can read the bucket and that CORS is set up correctly. You can select **Test connection** to check without saving. Then select **Add bucket** [S3].

- **Regular Python functions (`@weave.op`):** Put the URI string, such as `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/photos/cat.png`, in any input or output field. The field name doesn't matter, and you don't need to mark the field as media [S4, S7]. You'll see the pictures in Weave Traces.

The file extension decides how the URI displays. Common image types such as `.png`, `.jpg` and `.gif` show inline. Formats Weave doesn't display inline appear as a download link [S7]. If Weave can't resolve a URI, for example because the object is missing or the bucket isn't registered, the agent view shows the plain URI text instead [S8].

## Log a media reference using agent spans

Return a bucket URI as an agent tool result and Weave renders it inline in the **Agents** view, on the tool call that produced it. The following example opens a conversation, a turn, and a tool span, and sets a bucket URI as the tool's result. Replace `[YOUR-TEAM]`, `[YOUR-PROJECT]`, and `[YOUR-BUCKET]` with your own values.

import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

# A tool that returns an object that already lives in your bucket.
def get_frame(frame_id: int) -> str:
    return f"s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/frames/{frame_id:06d}.png"

        with weave.start_tool(
            name="get_frame",
            arguments='{"frame_id": 123}',
            tool_call_id="call_1",
        ) as tool:
            # The result is a bucket URI string; it renders inline in the Agents view.
            tool.result = get_frame(123)

> Render images and video that live in your own cloud bucket in the Weave Agents view by returning their URIs from agent tool spans, without importing the bytes into Weave.

Use this technique when the media you want to see in Weave already lives in your own bucket:

* Frames from a video pipeline.
* Screenshots from a browser agent.
* Images a model wrote to S3.

Instead of re-uploading those bytes into Weave, you log the object's URI as a string and Weave renders the image or video inline from your bucket. Only the URI is sent to Weave; the bytes stay in your bucket. Logging a 2 GB video costs the same as logging its path.

This is different from logging media with the [Content API](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/core-types/media.md#contents-api), which reads the bytes and stores them in Weave.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This is a Weave feature and is separate from [platform BYOB (secure storage connector)](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/secure-storage-connector.md), which backs W\&B artifact and run storage. Reference media buckets are configured per team and only need read access.

result.text:
## Register the reference bucket

Register the bucket in your team settings so Weave can presign and display referenced URIs.

1. Go to your team settings page (`https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/settings`).
2. In the **Reference buckets** section, select **Add bucket**.
3. Select your cloud provider (**AWS** or **Google Cloud**).
4. For the bucket name, enter `[YOUR-BUCKET]` only — without the `s3://` or `gs://` prefix.
5. For the object key, enter the key of an existing object in the bucket, for example `photos/cat.png` (the object key only, not a full URL). W\&B reads this one object to confirm it has read access and that CORS is configured correctly. This checks access only; once verified, presigning works for any object in the bucket.
6. Optionally, select **Test connection** to validate the configuration without saving.
7. Select **Add bucket** to save.

![The Add reference bucket dialog in team settings, with fields for the cloud provider, the bucket name, and an existing object key, plus Test connection and Add bucket buttons.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/add-ref-bucket.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=7ab906b46a48b51e085530aaaf1e47a4)

> [!WARNING]
>
> Until the bucket is registered, referenced URIs do not render. Registration is what lets Weave presign and display the object.

result.text:
## Prerequisites

* This feature is supported in [W\&B Multi-tenant Cloud](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/hosting-options/multi_tenant_cloud.md) and in preview for [Dedicated Cloud](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/hosting-options/dedicated-cloud.md) and [Self-Managed](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/hosting-options/self-managed.md) v0.84.0+.
* A CoreWeave Forge account and [API key](https://forge.coreweave.com/settings#apikeys).
* A cloud storage bucket you control (S3 or GCS), containing at least one object.
* Organization admin permissions. Adding a reference bucket requires the same permission as creating a team in the organization.

result.heading: How it works
result.text:
## How it works

Reference media rendering works in three steps:

1. You store a media object in your bucket, for example `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/frames/000123.png`.
2. You log that URI as a string value anywhere in a trace: an Op input or output, or an agent tool result. The field name does not matter.
3. When you open the trace, Weave resolves the URI to a short-lived [presigned URL](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/data-security/presigned-urls.md) and renders it inline. The file extension decides how it renders. Common image formats (such as `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) and video formats (such as `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.webm`) render inline. Other formats render as a download link.

Weave only resolves URIs that point at a bucket registered for your team. Supported schemes are `s3://` and `gs://`.

## View the reference in Weave Agents

Open the conversation from the link that `weave.init()` prints. The referenced image or video renders inline in the **Agents** view, on the tool call that returned the URI. If Weave can't resolve a URI, for example because the object is missing or the bucket isn't registered, it shows the plain URI string.

The main step left is to **register the bucket as a reference bucket for your team** in Weave. After that, each path only needs to record the picture's `s3://` URI as a plain string. Weave doesn't upload the image. When you open a trace, it creates a short-lived signed download link and shows the picture from your bucket [S1, S7].

**Remaining setup**
- Make sure you have organization admin permission. Adding a reference bucket needs the same permission as creating a team. The feature works in Multi-tenant Cloud. It's in preview for Dedicated Cloud and for Self-Managed v0.84.0+ [S6].
- Go to `https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/settings`, open **Reference buckets**, then select **Add bucket**. Choose **AWS** and enter just the bucket name, without `s3://` [S3].
- Enter the key of one object that's already in the bucket, such as `photos/cat.png`. W&B reads that object to confirm it can read the bucket and that CORS is set up correctly. You can select **Test connection** to check without saving. Then select **Add bucket** [S3].
- Until the bucket is registered, the URIs won't render as pictures. Weave only resolves URIs in buckets registered for your team [S3, S7].

**What each path should record**
- **Regular Python functions (`@weave.op`):** Put the URI string, such as `s3://[YOUR-BUCKET]/photos/cat.png`, in any input or output field. The field name doesn't matter, and you don't need to mark the field as media [S4, S7]. You'll see the pictures in Weave Traces.
- **Agent tools:** Inside `weave.start_conversation` → `weave.start_turn` → `weave.start_tool`, set `tool.result` to the URI string. The picture appears in the **Agents** view, on the tool call that returned it [S5, S8].

The file extension decides how the URI displays. Common image types such as `.png`, `.jpg` and `.gif` show inline. Formats Weave doesn't display inline appear as a download link [S7]. If Weave can't resolve a URI, for example because the object is missing or the bucket isn't registered, the agent view shows the plain URI text instead [S8].
